summary: A dense, interlocking worker-placement engine-builder where you cycle two types of workers around a rondel to gather resources, climb the temple, build structures, weave textiles, and muster an army to seize villages. It rewards careful long-term planning and combo-building far more than it rewards reacting to opponents.
praised: Tightly interlocking systems that all feed into each other in satisfying ways
High variability from modular setup, keeping replays fresh
Attractive production and thematic Inca art direction
Rewarding sense of engine-building and long-term strategy payoff
criticised: Steep learning curve and a dense rulebook that make the first game overwhelming
Long teach and play time, especially at 3-4 players
Mostly parallel play ("multiplayer solitaire") with limited direct interaction
Prone to analysis paralysis given the number of simultaneous tracks to optimize
Can feel more like an optimization puzzle than a thematic experience

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light area-majority conflict over village conquest

scoring.why: Points accumulate across temple steps, statues, buildings, weavings, and military area-majority conquests, so winners are usually those who build the most efficient multi-track engine rather than specialize in one
